title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters in event group chat
summary: Held because the PowerShell guidance describes -AllowedDomains as accepting a domain list, whereas Microsoft's reference requires a constructed domain object. The rollout dates and prerequisites match Microsoft's notice; two admin paths also need their final setting labels.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Users > External access reaches the page for managing external organizations.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Users > External access. Next to Teams and Skype for Business users in external organizations, choose Allow only specific external domains.
claims.fix: Complete controls[0].ui.path and the matching table path as 'Users > External access > Teams and Skype for Business users in external organizations > Allow only specific external domains > Add external domains', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-access. Keep the prose's shorter page reference.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowFederatedUsers $true enables tenant federation, subject to the separate domain and user-policy settings.
claims.quote: When set to True (the default value) users will be potentially allowed to communicate with users from other domains.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center External Collaboration left-rail section includes the existing External access page.
claims.quote: The External Collaboration section in the Teams Admin Center (TAC) left rail provides a unified location to manage all external collaboration settings. The section includes: ... External access: This is the existing page to manage configuration of federation

claims.claim: Organization-level external access settings govern the external organizations with which tenant users can chat and meet.
claims.quote: The organization settings apply to your entire organization. ... For meetings and chat with other Microsoft 365 organizations, you can specify which domains you want to trust.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Users > External access > Policies > policy reaches an external access policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Users > External access. Select the Policies tab. Click to add a policy or modify an existing one. Turn on Manage external domains for this policy to allow federation in the policy.
claims.fix: Complete controls[1].ui.path and the matching table path as 'Users > External access > Policies > policy > Manage external domains for this policy', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-access.

claims.claim: Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy -EnableFederationAccess $true is a Microsoft Teams PowerShell operation enabling federation access in the default policy.
claims.quote: Turn on the external domain management for the external access policy: Connect-MicrosoftTeams Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy -EnableFederationAccess $True

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP requires identity verification for external presenters joining events created under that policy.
claims.quote: To require external presenters to verify their identity before joining events created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the policy as still in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowedDomains parameter takes a domain list.
claims.quote: Note that string values cannot be passed directly to the AllowedDomains parameter. Instead, you must create an object reference using the New-CsEdgeAllowList cmdlet or the New-CsEdgeAllowAllKnownDomains cmdlet and then use the object reference variable as the parameter value.
claims.fix: Replace 'the -AllowedDomains and -BlockedDomains parameters take domain lists and are set in their own commands' with 'The -AllowedDomains parameter takes a domain object created with New-CsEdgeAllowList or New-CsEdgeAllowAllKnownDomains; -BlockedDomains takes a list. These are set separately from -AllowFederatedUsers.' Keep the existing reference citation: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-cstenantfederationconfiguration.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -BlockedDomains parameter accepts a domain list.
claims.quote: Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -BlockedDomains $list

claims.claim: The printed -AllowFederatedUsers command does not itself supply the allowed or blocked domain lists, which are configured separately.
claims.quote: Allow or prevent meetings and chat with other Teams organizations and Skype for Business | -AllowFederatedUsers | Specify allowed domains | -AllowedDomains | Specify blocked domains | -BlockedDomains
